title: An evening in the Emergency Department
intro: Clinical Immersion: six to nine in the evening with an emergency physician. You're in the short coat, with a pen light and a lot of questions.

steps.say: "Stick with me, stay out of the way of the stretchers, and ask me anything between patients. Wash your hands every time."
steps.speaker: Dr. Marcus Bell, emergency physician

steps.say: Bed 14, Super Track: a sixteen-year-old with an ankle injury from basketball, her mother holding the ice pack.
A tone sounds overhead: trauma alert, car versus pole, five minutes out. You follow Dr. Bell to Trauma 1, where the team is already gowning.
The patient arrives talking, which the team leader says out loud: the airway is open. The rest of the survey goes fast. He goes to CT with a broken arm and bruised ribs.
Room 6: an eighty-two-year-old woman from a nursing home, hot and confused, her blood pressure low.

steps.question: imm_ed_sepsis_01
steps.lead: "Sick or not sick? And what first?"

choice.prompt: In the hallway, the patient's son stops you. "You're a doctor, right? What's wrong with my mother?"

options.text: "I'm a medical student. I'll get Dr. Bell right now so he can talk with you."
options.reply: Dr. Bell comes straight out and takes him somewhere quiet to talk.

options.text: You tell him what you heard: probably sepsis from a urine infection.
options.reply: It's not your information to give, and not your role to give it.

options.text: "Sorry, I can't talk," and walk off.
options.reply: He's left alone in the corridor, frightened.

choice.lesson: Be clear about your role, and bring the right person to talk with families

steps.say: At nine, Dr. Bell signs your immersion form. "You didn't get in the way once. Come back when you're a third-year."

feedback: Dr. Bell writes: "Curious, careful, and knew when to step back."
Dr. Bell writes: "Engaged and eager. Keep reading around what you see."
Dr. Bell writes: "Good first shift. Read up on the cases tonight."
